prompt: A prism is $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{3}{4} \times 2$. Find its volume.
hint: Fraction side lengths still use length times width times height. Look for two factors that are easy to multiply first.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try it with whole numbers first: a $1 \times 3 \times 2$ prism has volume $6$. The same multiplying works with fractions.
Fraction side lengths still use length times width times height. Look for two factors that are easy to multiply first.
Notice that $\frac{1}{2} \times 2 = 1$. That leaves only $1 \times \frac{3}{4}$ to work out.
$\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{3}{4} \times 2 = \frac{3}{4}$, so the volume is $\frac{3}{4}$ cubic unit.

explanation: The volume of a prism is the product of its three dimensions: $V = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{3}{4} \times 2$.
You may multiply in any order, so pair $\frac{1}{2}$ with $2$ first because $\frac{1}{2} \times 2 = 1$.
What remains is the product $1 \times \frac{3}{4}$, and multiplying by one changes nothing, so it equals $\frac{3}{4}$.
The volume is $\frac{3}{4}$ cubic unit. Multiplying straight across gives $\frac{6}{8}$, which simplifies to the same value.
